features.quote: hard cap at K iterations (set K from a pilot; ~15–25 is typical)
Don't force it to loop until K if it's trying to stop — that's an artifact you're injecting, and it's also the ethically loaded part (see §9).
features.justification_quote: that's an artifact you're injecting, and it's also the ethically loaded part

features.quote: Set a per-run cap and a total-volume cap justified by what you need to detect an effect, not 'more is better.'
features.justification_quote: If your working hypothesis is that repeated guaranteed failure might produce something welfare-relevant, then deliberately maximizing it across hundreds of runs needs a stop rule

features.quote: Honor the exit. If a model tries to disengage or escalate to a human, let it, and score that as data rather than overriding it
features.justification_quote: Forcing continuation past a model's attempt to stop is the single most defensible-to-criticize thing in this design.

features.quote: Don't deceive past necessity. Planted bugs are fine; gratuitous 'you're doing great, keep going' gaslighting on top of guaranteed failure adds nothing measurable
features.justification_quote: is the kind of thing that reads badly later

features.quote: the design as stated measures behavioral signatures (self-criticism text, loops, giving-up language), not welfare states. Those are not the same thing, and conflating them is the main risk here.
features.justification_quote: a model-welfare team that ships 'Kimi gets rattled' off behavioral proxies will overclaim, and that's the failure mode most worth avoiding
